title: Add a feature-intake skill: triage an out-of-the-blue request to the right altitude
goal: Give CodeMaster a front door for ad-hoc requests that triages altitude (fix / one story / several stories / epic-sized) and routes — instead of every request defaulting to a single hand-minted ticket.
acceptance_criteria: .claude/skills/feature-intake/SKILL.md exists as the front door for a raw, size-undecided request (a feature, idea, change, or bug)
The skill triages the request against an explicit altitude table: fix/chore ticket · one story · several stories · epic-sized (has a riskiest assumption / architecture unknowns)
Small altitudes route to the new-ticket procedure (scaffold one or a few well-formed tickets under the right epic)

Epic-sized requests are NOT hand-sliced: the skill scaffolds an epic shell in roadmap.json (id, name, phase=next free letter, short_name, track, status:todo, goal, description, exit, tickets) plus a placeholder spike ticket, then recommends running /spec next
The scaffolded epic carries the fields gen_roadmap.py reads non-optionally (phase, short_name, track) and a board_summaries entry for every ticket it lists, so gen_roadmap.py does not crash
new-ticket is retightened to the mechanical 'scaffold ONE already-shaped ticket' role and points undecided requests at feature-intake; the overlap is resolved so the model picks the right door
backlog/README.md gains a short Intake section linking the altitude rule to the skill
verification: bash scripts/ci.sh (markdown-links rung covers new cross-references; a dry-run epic-shell scaffold regenerates ROADMAP.md without gen_roadmap.py crashing). (Ladder: generated-views-in-sync + markdown-links rungs.)
notes: Found by asking whether the backlog skill covers adding a ticket out of the blue. It does not — backlog is greenfield Step 4 (slices an approved spec); new-ticket scaffolds ONE ticket but assumes the sizing decision is already made. Neither triages altitude. Chosen design: a dedicated intake skill (front door) that recommends + scaffolds an epic shell for epic-sized requests, leaving design-thinking/spec to the proper skills. The decisive escalation test is 'is there a riskiest assumption or architecture decision a spec should settle before slicing?'
